question_text: The Indigenous People's Mandatory Representative (IPMR) of a municipality invokes RA 8371 (IPRA) to stop a mining company from operating within an ancestral domain. The company argues that it has a Mineral Production Sharing Agreement (MPSA) from the national government. Which of the following best supports the IPMR's position?

options.text: The IPRA grants indigenous communities absolute ownership over all mineral resources within ancestral domains.
The IPRA requires the free and prior informed consent (FPIC) of the indigenous community before any project can proceed within their ancestral domain.
The MPSA automatically overrides any ancestral domain claim because mining is a matter of national interest.
The IPRA only applies to ancestral lands, not ancestral domains, so the mining company can proceed.
